title: Synthesis of Thermogelling Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide)-graft-chondroitin Sulfate Composites with Alginate Microparticles for Tissue Engineering
protocol: Weigh out at least 10 g of NIPAAm monomer.
Dissolve the monomer in 400 ml of n-hexane at 60 °C.
Stir the container periodically until complete dissolution.
Recrystallize the solution in a -20 °C freezer for 24 hr.
Remove the crystallized monomer from the container and vacuum filter the n-hexane using a Buchner funnel.
Place the monomer in a vacuum oven at room temperature (RT) for 24 hr to remove any remaining n-hexane.
Store the monomer in a -20 °C freezer for later use.
Weigh out and dissolve 2.0 g of chondroitin sulfate in 8.0 ml of deionized water.
Gently heat the solution to 60 °C.
Adjust the pH of the solution to 10 using approximately 10 to 40 µl of 50% (w/w) NaOH.
Add 0.298 ml of methacrylic anhydride (MA).
Reflux for 24 hr while stirring at 60 °C.
Pour 400 ml of acetone solution into a jar and chill overnight in a -20 °C freezer.
After 24 hr have elapsed, slowly pour the entire methacrylated CS (mCS) solution into 400 ml of cold acetone while stirring with a magnetic stir bar.
Remove the mCS from the acetone and place the precipitate into a vacuum oven quickly to maintain an intact and cohesive state for mCS.
Allow the residual acetone to evaporate under vacuum for at least 24 hr.
Co-dissolve 10 g of purified NIPAAm and 2.209 g of mCS in 232 ml of deionized water.
Purge the solution with inert nitrogen gas for 15 min.
Add 0.976 ml of tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) to the purged solution.
Mix 97.6 mg of ammonium persulfate (APS) into the solution and seal it quickly.
Allow the solution to polymerize under fluorescent light for 24 hr.
Place the reaction vessel into a 37 °C oven after 24 hr.
Submerge the polymerized hydrogel in 1X phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) for 7 days.
Cut the hydrogel into small pieces, no greater than 5 cm in diameter, within the PBS solution at 37 °C.
Transfer portions of the hydrogel into 50 ml conical tubes.
Freeze the tubes at -70 °C for 1 to 2 hr.
Place the conical tubes on the freeze dryer.
Reach a temperature and pressure of approximately -40 °C and 0.04 mbar in the freeze dryer.
Remove all water from the hydrogel using the freeze dryer for at least 7 days.
Grind the freeze-dried polymer into a fine powder.
Store the powdered polymer in a refrigerator at 4 °C.
Prepare a 2% (w/v) alginate solution by dissolving 400 mg of alginate in 20 ml of deionized water.
Heat the alginate solution to approximately 60 °C to facilitate dissolution.
Prepare a 2% (w/v) calcium chloride solution by adding 400 mg of calcium chloride to 20 ml of deionized water.
Create an oil-in-water mixture by combining 100 ml of canola oil, 1.0 ml of Tween 20, and 20 ml of the 2% (w/v) alginate solution.
Emulsify the mixture for 10 minutes with a homogenizer at 15,000 rpm.
Mix the emulsion with a magnetic stir bar at either 200 rpm or 2,000 rpm to create large or small microparticles respectively.
Aspirate the calcium chloride solution using a syringe with an 18 G needle tip.
Slowly add the calcium chloride drop-wise into the emulsion until 20 ml of calcium chloride is exhausted.
Allow the microparticles within the emulsion to crosslink for 10 minutes.
Evenly distribute the batch of microparticles into capped 50 ml conical tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at a force of 1,400 x g for 2 minutes to remove canola oil.
Wash microparticles consecutively three times with isopropanol at 1,400 g for 2 min.
Discard the isopropanol supernatant after each centrifugation step.
Repeat washing procedure three additional times with deionized water.
Discard the deionized water supernatant after each centrifugation step.
Remove approximately 100 mg of wet microparticles and store in a vial.
Disperse a small sample of wet microparticles in deionized water on a microscope slide.
Adjust the numerical aperture until the particles come into focus using a 10X or 20X objective.
Measure the longest diameter of 50 random alginate microparticles with a line tool.
Obtain an average size for the batch based on measurements.
Wrap the microparticles with Kimwipes and secure them with rubber bands.
Freeze the microparticles at -70 °C for 1 hr.
Place the microparticles on the lyophilizer and allow drying for at least 24 hours.
Grind the freeze-dried microparticles into a fine powder using a mortar and pestle.
Store the ground microparticle powder in a refrigerator at 4°C.
Create a 5% (w/v) PNIPAAm-g-CS solution by dissolving 50 mg of hydrogel powder in 1 ml of 1x PBS.
Mix the PNIPAAm-g-CS solution using a vortex and chill it in a refrigerator at 4°C for 24 hours.
Add 25 or 50 mg of freeze-dried alginate microparticles to the chilled PNIPAAm-g-CS solution.
Vortex the mixture to create a homogenous composite adhesive.
Store the composite adhesive in a refrigerator at 4°C for later use.
Defrost a porcine ear in a warm 0.9% (w/v) NaCl solution.
Isolate and section off a flat, rectangular area of cartilage using a scalpel.
Cut vertically through the epidermal layer, subcutaneous tissue, and cartilage to isolate the cartilage substrate.
Separate the epidermal layer from the cartilage by cutting parallel through the subcutaneous tissue.
Carefully scrape the subcutaneous tissue attached to the cartilage using the side of the scalpel, avoiding cutting into the cartilage.
Ensure only one side of the cartilage is exposed and flat during tensile testing by cutting off uneven skin if necessary.
Cut the cartilage tissue into 1 cm x 1 cm pieces.
Store the cartilage in conical tubes filled with 0.9% (w/v) NaCl solution at -20°C.
Prepare 2.0 L of 0.9% (w/v) NaCl solution and preheat to 37°C.
Defrost frozen cartilage.
Keep porcine cartilage and hydrogel samples in a Styrofoam container with ice packs.
Attach the force gauge to the test stand arm.
Place a hotplate on top of the force stand and set to 50°C.
Affix a 1 cm x 1 cm piece of cartilage to the stainless steel block using cyanoacrylate glue and tweezers.
Glue an additional piece of cartilage to the Delrin cylinder and attach it to the force gauge, ensuring both surfaces face each other and contact the hydrogel.
Place the Plexiglas water bath on top of the hot plate and insert the stainless steel block with the cartilage substrate inside the bath.
Lower the arm of the test stand.
Align both cartilage substrates with one another.
Raise the arm and leave enough room to apply the hydrogel.
Dispense 200 µl of bioadhesive hydrogel to the bottom piece of cartilage using a positive displacement pipette.
Lower the arm of the force stand at 1 mm/min until the hydrogel contacts the upper piece of cartilage and exerts a preload force of 0.001 N.
Pour the 37 °C saline solution into the bath until reaching the designated water level.
Check the temperature of the solution with a thermocouple.
Allow the hydrogel to set for a total of 5 minutes.
Raise the arm at a speed of 2 mm/min once the gel has solidified.
Collect recorded data and raise the arm of the test stand.
Remove the Delrin cylinder from the force gauge.
Pour the saline solution back into its previous container.
Reheat the saline solution to 37 °C.
Calculate stresses by subtracting the force exerted by the polymer from the buoyant force of a "blank" and dividing by the bond area.
Prepare clean glass vials.
Label glass vials appropriately with time point, sample type, and sample number.
Pre-weigh all glass vials and record their initial mass at room temperature (RT).
Dispense approximately 0.4 ml of the prepared adhesive sample into each of five vials using a syringe.
Weigh and record the mass of each vial containing the adhesive sample at RT.
Pre-warm an orbital incubator to 37 °C.
Prepare 1 L of 1x PBS solution and pre-warm it to 37 °C.
Organize all vials on a rack and insert the rack into the incubator.
Allow adhesives to transition from liquid to gel for approximately 5 to 10 minutes.
Add 5.0 ml of 1x PBS to each vial carefully along the side of the vial.
Cap each vial to prevent evaporation of the PBS solution and maintain internal temperature at 37 °C.
Maintain each set of hydrogel discs submerged in PBS for a designated length of time.
At the 7 day time point, uncap the set of vials.
Remove the PBS solution from each vial.
Weigh each vial containing the adhesive sample again at RT.
Grow human embryonic kidney 293 cells (HEK-293) to 80% confluence.
Quick-thaw the frozen HEK-293 cell suspension by placing the cryovial in a 37 °C water bath.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 x g at 4 °C for 5 min in a 15 ml conical tube.

Combine high glucose (4.5 g/L) Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM), heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (FBS) to a final concentration of 20%, and the 100x penicillin-streptomycin solution (pen-strep) to a final concentration of 100 I.U/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin for the first passage cell growth medium.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 ml of growth medium.
Transfer the suspension into one 100 mm diameter petri dish.
Evenly distribute the cells by gently tilting the dish front to back and left to right a few times each direction.
Culture the cells in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium every two days if necessary.
When cells reach 80% confluency, replicate the culture into multiple dishes.
Remove the medium from the plate.
Add 1 ml of 0.5% trypsin to the plate.
Allow the plates to incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Gently swirl the plate to check if the cells detach from the surface.
For splitting the culture 1:10, add 9 ml of regular growth medium (DMEM with 10% FBS) to the trypsinized cells.
Gently mix by tilting the dish.
Dispense 1 ml of the diluted cell suspension into each new dish.
Add 9 ml of growth medium to each dish.
Gently mix by tilting the dish.
Culture the cells in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium every two days until cells reach 80% confluence.
Remove the media from two culture dishes grown to 80% confluence.
Add 1 ml of 0.5% trypsin to each plate.
Allow the plates to incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Check if the cells detach by gently swirling the plate.
Wash the HEK-293 cells on the plate with 3 ml of growth medium twice and add both suspensions to a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the 15 ml conical tube for 10 min at 400 x g at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 3 ml of medium by pipetting up and down.
Pipette 10 µl of the cell suspension into a hemocytometer and perform a cell count to determine the cell density.
Increase or decrease the volume of medium as needed to preserve a target concentration of 1 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Centrifuge the HEK-293 cells at 400 x g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the corrected volume of media accordingly.
Gently vortex the cell suspension.
Evenly distribute the cell mix into four separate 15 ml conical tubes for test conditions.
Pipette multiple 300 µl volumes of the cell mix into a 24-well plate to generate positive control monolayers with 4-6 replicate samples.
Remove the media from the conical tubes pertaining to the killed control, PNIPAAm-g-CS, and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles.
Centrifuge the conical tubes for 5 minutes at 400 x g.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells in the same volume of PNIPAAm-g-CS as the removed media to maintain cell concentration.
Pipette the polymer cell mix up and down using a serological pipette until homogenous.
Transfer the PNIPAAm-g-CS-cell suspension into a 35 mm culture dish if seeding with alginate microparticles.
Introduce the particles into the polymer-cell mix for alginate microparticle condition.
Pipette the cell mix up and down using a serological pipette until homogenous after introducing particles.
Dispense multiple 300 µl of the polymer cell mix into each well for killed control, PNIPAAm-g-CS, and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles to generate 4-6 replicate samples.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 10 to 15 min.
Position a slide warmer in the hood and set it to 37 °C.
Pipette 600 μl of pre-warmed media into each well.
Warm up the air above the dish with a lamp containing a fluorescent bulb.
Incubate cells for 5 days at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Defrost ethidium homodimer (EthD-1) and calcein AM from the kit at room temperature.
Add 5 ml of sterile 1x PBS to a conical tube.
Wrap the conical tube containing 5 ml of sterile 1x PBS in aluminum foil.
Add 6.67 μl of 2 mM EthD-1 to the conical tube.
Vortex the solution thoroughly.
Add 2.5 μl of 4 mM calcein AM to the conical tube.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Remove media from wells containing monolayer, PNIPAAm-g-CS, and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles.
Wash all wells gently with PBS.
Remove PBS from the wells.
Allow hydrogel discs containing alginate microparticles to liquefy at room temperature.
Add 2 ml of 50 mM sodium citrate to each well.
Remove the media from the killed cell wells (negative control).
Allow the hydrogel discs to liquefy at RT and add 300 μl of 70% methanol to each well.
Incubate the plate for 45 min at 37 °C.
Remove the sodium citrate and methanol solutions from the wells and pipette each of the hydrogel suspensions into individual microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 2,000 x g for 10 min to separate the cells from the hydrogel suspension.
Carefully remove the suspension by pipetting the solution from the conical tube and leaving behind the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 300 μl of PBS and transfer to the original well plate.
Add 300 μl of the Live/Dead dye mix to each of the wells.
Wrap the well plate in aluminum foil and incubate for 45 min on a rocker at RT.
Image all of the samples under an inverted fluorescence microscope with a 10X objective.
Grow HEK-293 cells to 80% confluence.
Remove the growth media from two culture dishes.
Add 1 ml of 0.5% trypsin to each plate.
Allow the plates to incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Check if the cells detach from the surface by gently swirling the plate.
Wash the HEK-293 cells on the plate with 3 ml of media twice and add both suspensions to the same 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the 15 ml conical tube for 10 min at 400 x g at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 ml of media by pipetting up and down.
Pipette 10 μl of the cell suspension into a hemocytometer to perform a cell count.
Determine the cell density and preserve a target concentration of 1 x 10^6 cells/ml.
Centrifuge the HEK-293 cells at 400 x g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the corrected volume of media accordingly.
Gently vortex the cell suspension to ensure uniform distribution.
Evenly distribute the cell mix into four separate 15 ml conical tubes for different test conditions.
Create positive control monolayers by pipetting 300 μl of the cell mix into a 24-well plate.
Generate 4 - 6 replicate samples for the positive control.
Remove the media from the conical tubes pertaining to the killed control, PNIPAAm-g-CS, and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles.
Centrifuge the conical tubes for 5 min at 400 x g.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Maintain the same cell concentration by resuspending the cells in the same volume of PNIPAAm-g-CS as the removed media.
Pipette the cell mix up and down using a serological pipette until homogenous.
Transfer the PNIPAAm-g-CS-cell suspension into a 35 mm culture dish.
Introduce alginate microparticles into the cell mix.
Pipette the cell mix up and down using a serological pipette until homogenous.
Dispense 300 μl of the polymer cell mix into each of the wells for killed control, PNIPAAm-g-CS, and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles to generate 4 - 6 replicate samples.
Dispense multiple 300 μl volumes of PNIPAAm-g-CS and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles without cells in adjacent wells to generate 4 - 6 replicate samples.
Incubate the 24-well plate at 37 °C for 10 to 15 min to allow the PNIPAAm-g-CS to transition from a liquid to a gel state.
Position a slide warmer in the hood and set the temperature to 37 °C.
Use the slide warmer to maintain well plate temperature.
Pipette 600 μl of pre-warmed clear DMEM into each well.
Position a lamp with a fluorescent bulb above the dish to warm up the air above it.
Incubate the cells for 5 days at 37 °C at 5% CO2.
Prepare the 2,3-bis-(2-methoxy-4-nitro-5-sulfophenyl)-2H-tetrazolium-5-carboxanilide (XTT) reagent from the manufacturer on the day of use.
Reconstitute XTT powder with 5 ml of clear DMEM through the rubber septum.
Heat the reagent to 56 °C in a water bath for 10 min until dissolved.
Dilute the XTT reagent to 20% (v/v) in a 15 ml conical tube wrapped in aluminum foil.
Aliquot excess XTT reagent into microcentrifuge tubes and store at -20 °C.
Remove media from killed cell wells and add 300 µl of 70% methanol to each well.
Incubate the methanol-treated wells for 45 min at 37 °C.
Remove methanol from the wells after incubation.
Remove media from remaining wells including positive control, PNIPAAm-g-CS, and PNIPAAm-g-CS with alginate microparticles.
Wash all of the wells thoroughly but gently with PBS.
Add 300 µl of 20% XTT reagent to each well.
Wrap the 24-well plate in aluminum foil and incubate on a rocker at RT for 24 hr.
After 24 hr, add 200 µl of 50 mM sodium citrate to all wells.
Incubate with sodium citrate on the rocker for an additional hour.
Transfer polymer suspensions from each well to microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 2,000 x g for 10 min at RT.
Transfer 200 µl of supernatant from each tube to a 96-well plate.
Obtain specific absorbance readings at 450 nm using a microtiter plate reader.
Obtain non-specific absorbance readings at 690 nm using the microtiter plate reader.
